title: The Yardstick
question: How will we know a model is good?
goals: Learn the new words, then load and look.
Split by time, and seal the last years.
Leave a gap as long as the label.
Build the tests inside the development years.
Fit every bound on the training rows only.
Sum up a ranking in one number.
Count what a review budget finds.
Put an interval on a score.
Measure the classic scores on the yardstick.
Refit the classic, then use every ratio.
Read the first three rungs of the ladder.

random_split.name: Holding out rows at random
random_split.naive_label: ROC-AUC, rows held out at random
random_split.why: A random split trains on the years it is tested on, and on the same companies a year apart.

trapezoid.name: Joining a precision-recall curve with straight lines
trapezoid.why: With few distinct scores the straight lines run far above the curve's true steps.

bootstrap.name: Drawing rows as if they were independent
bootstrap.naive_label: Width of the 95% interval, rows drawn
bootstrap.honest_label: Width of the 95% interval, companies drawn
bootstrap.why: A company brings several rows that move together, so rows carry less news than their count.
